script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for June 10. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Before you speak a word, your clothes have already spoken.  They announce your profession, your tribe, your status, your mood.  Every choice—formal or casual, colorful or plain—sends a message.

Throughout history, clothing marked social rank. Sumptuary laws restricted who could wear what. Purple for emperors. Silk for nobles. Today's status symbols are subtler—designer labels, quality materials—but still communicate hierarchy. We dress to belong.  Business suits, punk leather, hippie tie-dye, athletic wear—each is a tribal uniform saying 'I'm one of you.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Everything we choose communicates something.  Clothing teaches that there is no neutral presentation—even trying not to send a message sends a message.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Clothing Audit - What Are You Saying?.

Here's your activity: Look at what you're wearing right now. What message does it send? What assumptions would a stranger make? Does your clothing match what you want to communicate? Dress deliberately tomorrow—choose clothes that say what you intend. This helps you increase awareness of clothing as communication.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what clothes communicate can be applied to clothing audit - what are you saying?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
